a.d: Used to ask back in astonishment, reconfirming what was just heard because it is shocking or hard to believe.
ex: 그 성실하던 팀장님이 회사를 갑자기 **그만두신다고요**? / You say that diligent team leader is suddenly resigning?

b.d: Used to convey a reported fact neutrally to a third party without personal emotional reaction.
ex: 팀장님이 다음 달에 퇴사하신**다고 해요**. / They say the team leader is retiring next month.

im-c52-01.tip: Use -다고요? with rising intonation to express surprise or check what your ears just caught.

im-c52-01.q: Fix the unnatural sentence that uses a flat declarative report instead of asking back in surprise upon hearing startling news.
im-c52-01.wrong: 내일 비행기가 태풍 때문에 결항되었다고 해요? (놀라며 되물을 때)
answers: 내일 비행기가 태풍 때문에 결항되었다고요?
내일 비행기가 태풍 때문에 결항되었다고요

태풍 때문에 내일 비행기가 결항되었다고요
im-c52-01.hint: When asking back in disbelief upon hearing unexpected news, use -다고요?: 결항되었다고요?
im-c52-01.why: Expressing surprise and seeking reconfirmation calls for the reactive interrogative -다고요?.

im-c52-02.h: -다고 하던데 (Hearsay Background for Suggestion) vs -다고 해요 (Simple Relay)

a.h: -다고 하던데 (Citing heard information to set up a suggestion)
a.d: Used to cite a rumor, recommendation, or report as the background premise before proposing a related action or question.
ex: 그 영화가 아주 **재미있다고 하던데** 이번 주말에 보러 갈까요? / They say that movie is very fun, shall we go watch it this weekend?

b.d: Used merely to relay what someone else said without attaching a personal invitation or suggestion.
ex: 친구가 그 영화가 **재미있다고 해요**. / My friend says that movie is fun.

im-c52-02.tip: Use -다고 하던데 (contracted to -다던데) followed by suggestions: -ㄹ까요?, -러 가요, -아/어 보세요.

im-c52-02.q: Fix the awkward phrasing when proposing to visit a restaurant based on heard reputation.

im-c52-02.hint: Citing heard praise to propose an outing takes -다고 하던데 (or -다던데) with -ㄹ까요?: 맛있다고 하던데 오늘 가 볼까요?
im-c52-02.why: Framing secondhand information as the conversational premise for a proposal calls for -다고 하던데.

a.d: Used when confirming a piece of news already heard, usually with a warm, encouraging, or congratulatory tone.
ex: 시험에 **합격했다면서요**? 진심으로 축하드려요! / I heard you passed the exam? Congratulations from the bottom of my heart!

b.d: Used when astounded, disappointed, or expressing indignant disbelief at shocking unexpected news.
ex: 아무런 사전 예고 없이 **그만두신다니요**? / Resigning without any advance notice? What is going on?

im-c52-03.tip: Use -다면서요? to confirm good news and celebrate; use -다니요? to push back against shocking or dismaying reports.

im-c52-03.why: -다니요? conveys shock, dismay, or protest; warmly confirming good news requires -다면서요?.

items: I can confirm heard news warmly to celebrate colleagues using -다면서요?.

a.d: Used to validate positive achievements, creating an uplifting social atmosphere.

im-c52-04.tip: Match the tone: -다면서요? carries warmth and celebration; -다니요? carries indignation, bewilderment, or disbelief.

en: In Korean conversation, chiming in to the news your partner shares with appropriate quote endings is extremely important.
Celebrate welcome news with '-다면서요?', and express empathy for hard-to-believe shocks with '-다니요?' or '-다고요?'.
Delicate reactions tailored to situations become the key that enriches conversation and builds deep rapport.

Staring into space without saying anything
Changing the subject completely whenever someone speaks
